title: An algebraic stack with setoid fibres is an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use categories fibred in groupoids, their morphisms and 2-morphisms as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], algebraic spaces as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $\mathcal W$ be an fppf stack in groupoids over $S$: its isomorphism presheaves are fppf sheaves and all fppf descent data for objects are effective. Suppose its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, meaning that every scheme 2-base change of the diagonal is equivalent to an algebraic space, and that it admits a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas. Smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; surjectivity means lifting field-valued objects after field extension [def-weil-field]. Assume that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $x,y\in\mathcal W(T)$ the set of arrows $x\to y$ has at most one element (the fibres are setoids). Then there exists an algebraic space $E/S$ and an equivalence over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ from $\mathcal W$ to the discrete fibred groupoid $T\mapsto E(T)$.

proof.text: Every etale covering is an fppf covering: its arrows are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and joint surjectivity is unchanged in [def-pc-fppf-site]. Therefore the assumed fppf sheaf condition for isomorphisms and effectiveness of object descent hold on etale coverings. The diagonal condition and the smoothness of the atlas are word for word those of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. For surjectivity, fix $h_T\to\mathcal W$, let $Z\simeq h_T\times_{\mathcal W}h_U$ be the algebraic space and $V\to Z$ a representable surjective etale scheme chart [def-trf-algebraic-space]; surjectivity of $Z\to T$ means that of $V\to T$. If field-valued objects lift, take $t\in T$ and the restriction of the object to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-field]: a lift over $L\supseteq\kappa(t)$ is an $L$-point of $Z$ over $t$, and $V\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is surjective, so some point of $V$ maps to $t$. Conversely, for $x\in\mathcal W(K)$ take $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$; then $V\neq\emptyset$, and a point $v\in V$ gives $L=\kappa(v)\supseteq K$ and an object of $U(L)$ with an isomorphism of its image to $x|_L$. Hence the hypotheses give precisely the algebraic-stack predicate of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], with the same atlas and the same scheme base changes.

source.place: Tag 026O, definition-algebraic-stack and the following comparison with the etale convention.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $x\in\mathcal W(T)$, the identity $1_x$ exists. Every automorphism $a:x\to x$ equals $1_x$, since the assumed arrow set has at most one element. This verifies the automorphism hypothesis on every test scheme, including nonreduced ones, rather than only on geometric points.

Apply the existing theorem [lem-sfb-algebraic-setoid-space] to $\mathcal X=\mathcal W$ with the algebraic-stack predicate from step 1 and the automorphism condition from step 2. It supplies an algebraic space $E/S$ and an equivalence $h_E\simeq\mathcal W$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Take the inverse equivalence to obtain $\mathcal W\simeq h_E$. Here $h_E(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,E)$ is discrete, exactly the required fibred groupoid.
